text:
sre-oncall: Heads up — we're seeing a networking degradation in us-east-1 impacting instance-to-instance connectivity and cross-AZ traffic. Affected: gpu-cluster-prod-1 and several BGP routes. KMS calls intermittently failing with 5xx decrypt errors. Investigating cause with cloud provider now.

maria (infra): Confirmed. Telemetry shows packet drops between AZa <-> AZb since ~12:40 UTC, instance metrics show elevated TCP retransmits. Some GPU nodes lost heartbeats to orchestrator, autoscaler draining a few nodes.

alex (eng-runtime): This is causing higher inference latencies (tail p95->p99) and KV cache misses. Streaming requests are getting 502s intermittently. We should consider routing traffic away from us-east-1 for hosted API and throttling Dedicated bursts.

jen (security): KMS decrypt failures are concerning. Are we seeing a specific error code? If it's 5xx on provider side, do we have a fallback for cached encryption keys? Need to avoid any key material exposure.

maria (infra): Error: "KMS.Decrypt.InternalError" and "ThrottlingException" combos. Some requests succeed. We have short-lived wrapped keys in the node-local cache — we can extend cache TTL to 60m for emergency to avoid rekeying requests, but need security signoff.

jen (security): I'm ok with emergency TTL increase if we rotate afterwards and add audit notes. Post an incident log entry and I'll approve. :+1:

ops-bot: deploy-notice: Autoscaler draining nodes in gpu-cluster-prod-1 (group gpu-pool-3) at 12:47 UTC.

alex (eng-runtime): Plan suggestion: 1) Shift API traffic off us-east-1 -> us-east-2 for hosted routes; 2) For Dedicated customers pinned to us-east-1, enable per-customer fallback to less-sensitive model variants in other regions (configurable); 3) Increase local KMS cache TTL to 60m for nodes with cached keys; 4) Set autoscaler to conservative mode (no aggressive scale-up) to avoid spiking provisioning while network unstable.

kyle (product): How much capacity can us-east-2 absorb? We need to estimate degraded throughput vs cost. Also notify customers via status page if their SLA might be affected.

maria (infra): us-east-2 has ~60% free GPU capacity right now (nv48 pools). We can shift up to ~40% of typical peak traffic without triggering spot/provisioning. Beyond that we'd incur provisioning delays/cost.

paul (support): Start drafting a status update copy: mention "partial networking degradation in us-east-1 affecting inference latency and some API errors. Failover in progress." Want me to post?

jen (security): Also: for Private deployments using customer-managed KMS/HSM, check if their KMS endpoints are reachable — if not, they'll see similar decrypt failures. Notify account teams.

maria (infra): Reached AWS: they've acknowledged a networking fabric issue affecting some AZ peering in us-east-1, currently P2, engineer assigned, ETA unknown (they said investigating internal routing). I've requested priority escalation citing KMS and high-impact services.

alex (eng-runtime): Immediate commands I ran for routing (devops runbook):
```
# shift traffic for hosted API route set
redwoodctl routes update --service hosted-api --region us-east-1 --preferred-regions us-east-2 --weight 0.0
# set autoscaler conservative
redwoodctl autoscale set --pool gpu-pool-3 --min 6 --max 12 --policy conservative
```
Use these if you have perms.

sre-oncall: I'm going to start applying traffic weight changes incrementally (+10% every 2 min) to avoid sudden capacity spikes. Will monitor p50/p95/p99 and error rates.

ops-bot: incident-log: Incident created — id INC-2026-0318-07, severity: high, owner: sre-oncall.

kyle (product): Draft for status page (short): "We are investigating a partial networking degradation in us-east-1 impacting inference latency and causing transient errors for some customers. Failover and mitigation steps are in progress. We will post updates every 15 minutes." Approve?

paul (support): Approved. Posting now to status.redwood.ai and customer Slack channels for enterprise customers.

jen (security): After we enable local TTL increase, add an automated audit event and create a follow-up ticket to rotate cached keys and force re-decrypt once KMS stable. Also notify compliance.

maria (infra): Executed KMS cache TTL bump on affected node group (gpu-pool-3): set ttl 3600s. Creating follow-up runbook: INC-2026-0318-07 -> RM-rotate-keys.

alex (eng-runtime): Observability: p50 stable, p95 improved after start of shift, p99 still elevated. Error rate dropping from 6% -> 1.2% after 30m of incremental reroutes. KV cache hitrate improved after TTL bump.

aws-status-bot: AWS: We are investigating an issue with networking in US-EAST-1 that may impact service connectivity. (https://status.aws.amazon.com/)

maria (infra): Cost note: if we keep >20% traffic in us-east-2 for >24h, estimate ~15% increase in infra spend due to cross-region egress and provisioning buffer. Flagging for finance.

kyle (product): Put a temporary cost cap alert and notify sales for larger Dedicated customers that may see bill changes.

paul (support): Customer comms sent to enterprise list: "We're failing over traffic to adjacent region; performance should stabilize but you may see degraded throughput for a short window. Our team will follow up."

sre-oncall: Monitoring — will send next update at +15m or on material change. If AWS provides ETA we'll decide on permanent routing for the remainder of the day. Thanks all. :heart:

jen (security): One more — review HSM connectivity for on-prem/private customers: get account owners to confirm local KMS is reachable and fallback keys exist.

maria (infra): Noted, pinging account owners and ops leads.

alex (eng-runtime): Follow-up checklist I've created: [1] Confirm AWS network fix; [2] Drain and reprovision affected GPU nodes after fix; [3] Rotate keys and shrink TTL; [4] Replay traffic tests; [5] Postmortem owner assignment.

ops-bot: incident-update: INC-2026-0318-07 - AWS escalated to network ops, ETA unknown. Next update in 15m."
